note: *** Mother of MANUEL LERENA LEONARD ***, named with her husband *** PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA *** on their son's 1890 marriage and his 1926 death registration. *** HER SURNAME IS THE SOURCE OF HIS COMPOUND, AND HER OWN CIVIL ACT SPELLS IT LEONAR, 17 October 2026. *** The remark this row made on 11 October - that LEONARD is an English, Irish or French name and she the first such woman in the Uruguayan line - IS WITHDRAWN: it was a guess about a surname read off a son's index, and her own act gives no origin for it. Her father is written Antonio Leonar and she was born in Montevideo. *** CONFIRMED, 17 OCTOBER 2026: SHE IS THE WIDOW BURIED AT THE CORDON ON 27 AUGUST 1901. *** Her CIVIL death registration, no. 252 of the same day, read at the plate: margin 'Teresa Leonar de Lerena'; she died 'a las dos de la manana del dia de hoy' in the house calle Particular 6 (altos), 'de nacionalidad oriental, nacida en esta Ciudad, de sesenta anos de edad, de estado VIUDA', of endocarditis by the certificate of a Dr V. Tagle; 'hija legitima de Antonio Leonar [a word follows that may be 'catalan'], fallecido, y de MANUELA ITURRIAGA, de 82 anos, viuda, oriental, con domicilio en la misma casa del suceso; y que era viuda de Pedro Antonio Lerena, oriental, quedando del matrimonio un hijo llamado: Manuel.' *** SO SHE WAS BORN ABOUT 1841, HER MOTHER WAS STILL ALIVE AT EIGHTY-TWO, HER HUSBAND WAS DEAD BY AUGUST 1901, AND THE CORDON CLERK WROTE HER SURNAME 'LEONOR' - the plate of the burial reads Leonor, which this row had taken for a given name. *** Declared by 'Manuel Lerena', married, oriental, a soldier (militar), of the 8th section, about thirty-eight - her son - and by Eduardo Epifanio Alvarez, single, an employee. *** HER HUSBAND IS NOT PEDRO LERENA VEGA - SETTLED, 17 October 2026, FROM THE PLATE OF THEIR DAUGHTER'S BAPTISM. *** The christening of MANUELA, born 9 April 1864 and baptised 30 April 1864 at the Catedral, reads 'hija legitima de Pedro Lerena y de Teresa Leonar. Abuelos Paternos Pedro y Maria Pereyra. Maternos Antonio y Manuela Barriaga. Padrinos Jose Paredes y Manuela Barriaga'. HER HUSBAND'S MOTHER WAS MARIA PEREYRA; Pedro Lerena Vega's mother was Vicenta Vega. THEY ARE TWO MEN, and Manuela Lemos and Teresa Leonar were wives of two different Pedros. Teresa had at least TWO children - Manuel, and Manuela in 1864 - and the 1901 act, which names only a son, does not mention a daughter. *** A HOMONYM, 17 OCTOBER 2026 - DO NOT MERGE AND DO NOT ATTACH: *** a SECOND 'Teresa Leonar' is at Montevideo in 1871-74, wife of TOMAS BALINAS (the index and the plate give Balinas, Ballinas), mother of Fermin Rodolfo, born in July 1871 and christened at La Union in May 1874: 'hijo legitimo de Tomas Balinas y Teresa Leonar, orientales: abuelos paternos Tomas y Maria Torres: abuelos maternos ANTONIO Y MANUELA ORTIN'. *** HER FATHER'S NAME IS THE SAME AS THIS TERESA'S (Antonio Leonar) AND HER MOTHER'S SURNAME IS NOT: *** the plate reads Ortin, where this Teresa's civil act reads Iturriaga and her daughter's 1864 christening reads Marriaga/Barriaga. *** THEY ARE PROBABLY TWO WOMEN *** - two daughters of one father given one name would be odd, a half-sister by a second Manuela odder still, and the 1901 act names only a widowhood of Pedro Antonio Lerena and a son Manuel - but a remarriage, or an Iturriaga/Ortin confusion of the clerks, is not excluded and no document settles it. *** A FAMILY-TREE PROFILE 'TERESA LEONAR ORTIN, BORN 1840' HAS ALREADY BEEN ATTACHED TO THE 1874 RECORD: *** unsourced, not used, and a warning that a tree may merge the two. *** HER MARRIAGE IS FOUND AS A PETITION, 18 October 2026: SHE WAS BETROTHED TO DON PEDRO A. LERENA IN JUNE 1861. *** 'Illmo y Rmo Sor Vicario. Don Pedro A. Lerena, ante V.S. con el debido respeto me presento y expongo: que habiendo concertado contraer matrimonio segun orden de nuestra Santa Madre la Iglesia con Dona Teresa Leonard, parroquiana de la Matriz, y siendo imposible esperar la publicacion de las tres proclamas por tener que [ausentarse] la madre de la contrayente, [que] paso al campo a asistir una hija enferma, vengo a suplicar a V.S. quiera servirse acordarme la dispensa de dos conciliares proclamas', signed 'Pedro A. Lerena'; the decree 'Montevideo, Junio 8 de 1861' (the day is CONFIRMED by the Vicario's own register of dispensations, no. 422: 'El ocho de Junio de mil ochocientos sesenta y uno, S.S. dispenso a Don Pedro Antonio Lerena dos conciliares proclamas en el matrimonio que intenta contraer con Da. Teresa Leonard, parroquiana de la Matriz'): 'Vistos, y considerando lo expuesto, dispensamos, como se pide, [dos] proclamas', with the petition sent to be entered in the register of dispensations as no. 422. *** SHE IS 'DONA TERESA LEONARD, PARROQUIANA DE LA MATRIZ' *** - the Catedral's parish, where her daughter was christened in 1864 - AND HER MOTHER WAS AWAY AT THE CAMPO NURSING A SICK DAUGHTER: so Teresa HAD A SISTER, ill in the country in June 1861, whom no document names. *** THE MARRIAGE ACT ITSELF IS STILL NOT FOUND *** (no index entry under Leonard, Leonar or Leonor), but it falls soon after the decree, which is three years before Manuela's christening and fits a first child at that time. The petition spells her surname LEONARD - the spelling this row has used since it was entered - and gives no age.

The first item appraised is *** 'un RANCHO de veinte y dos varas de largo, siete de ancho, con las paredes de PIEDRA, revocadas y blanqueadas de ambas partes, con CUATRO VIVIENDAS, la una de ellas compuesta de PULPERIA con mostrador, armazon y adyacentes, trastienda, sala y aposento' ***. Then a house of *** six doors, three with lock and fittings, and five windows ***, paved floor and corridors on both sides - *** 746 pesos ***; a stone-walled, thatch-roofed building of eleven varas by seven - *** 314 pesos ***; and *** 'una ATAHONA compuesta de casa, rueda, piedras, palo-fierro, linterna y demas utensilios' *** - a *** MILL *** - at *** 310 pesos ***. Then the tools: stone-picks, an adze, axes, a turned round table, benches, a pine chest, a crowbar, a spade, a hoe. *** SO THE MAN WHOSE ESTATE RAMON LERENA WAS SENT TO VALUE KEPT THE SHOP AND THE MILL OF HIS DISTRICT *** - which is also why the case was worth a court in Buenos Aires taking an interest in. *** HIS MINOR SON IS NEVER NAMED IN THE FRAMES READ ***, only ever 'su hijo menor'. *** HE DIED SIX YEARS EARLIER THAN THIS ROW'S NAME SAYS - BY 1794, NOT BY 1800. *** The 1794 file already calls him *** 'el finado Don CLEMENTE GARCIA' *** and already calls Celestina Gonzalez *** 'la viuda' ***. *** THE ROW'S OWN TITLE IS NOW WRONG AND IS LEFT UNCHANGED DELIBERATELY ***, because renaming a person changes their published address; see data/corrections.tsv and the slug ledger. *** AND HE HAD AN ESTANCIA AS WELL AS THE SHOP AND THE MILL. *** The 1794 inventory walks out to *** 'la ESTANCIA del finado' *** to count *** 'EL GANADO Y CABALLOS' ***. So the estate is a rural holding with stock, a store, a mill and a house - *** which is why it took two inventories six years apart and a court in the capital. ***

AND IT PUTS HIM IN SANCHO'S HOUSE. *** *** 'En VEINTE Y TRES DE JUNIO de mil ochocientos OCHENTA, el Presbitero Don JUAN JOSE BRID, con licencia del Cura Parroco de esta BASILICA MENOR Y CATEDRAL DE MONTEVIDEO, DISPENSADAS LAS TRES CONCILIARES PROCLAMAS por el Ilustrisimo y Reverendisimo Senor Obispo Diocesano DON JACINTO VERA, autorizo... el matrimonio que contrajo el DOCTOR DON ARTURO [L]ERENA, natural de esta Republica, soltero, de VEINTE Y DOS ANOS de edad, HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON AVELINO LERENA Y DONA AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con DONA EMMA REGULES... de DIEZ Y SEIS ANOS de edad, hija legitima de DON WENCESLAO REGULES y DONA JUSTINIANA MELILLA: fueron testigos el DOCTOR DON AMBROSIO LERENA y Dona Justiniana Melilla de Regules.' *** *** SO HE IS A SON OF AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - See data/_person-pairs.txt. *** A LEAD NOT YET OPENED: *** the Montevideo civil marriages of 1907-08 carry a *** 'Dona EMMA LERENA REGULES' *** with her parents given as 'don Arturo Lerena' and 'Emma Regules' - a daughter, marrying. *** HE IS A LAWYER, NOT A PHYSICIAN - AND THIS ROW SAID 'DOCTOR' FOR AN HOUR WITHOUT ASKING WHICH KIND. *** His daughter's marriage act of 9 August 1909 gives him plainly: *** 'hija de don ARTURO LERENA, de estado casado, DE PROFESION ABOGADO, de nacionalidad oriental, domiciliado en la calle COLONIA 2200' ***. In Uruguay *** DOCTOR IS THE STYLE OF AN ABOGADO *** as much as of a medico, and the 1880 marriage act's 'el Doctor Don Arturo Lerena' carries no more than that. *** THE OCCUPATION FIELD IS CORRECTED AND SO IS THE INFERENCE DRAWN FROM IT ***: this archive wrote that the Lerena Traibel were 'a professional household' on the strength of two men called Doctor, which remains true, and said it in a way that suggested medicine, which was never stated. *** A SECOND CHILD, 12 October 2026: *** *** EMMA LERENA REGULES, born 18 May 1885 at SAN JOSE ***, who married Fermin Carlos de Yeregui at Montevideo on 9 August 1909. *** SO THE HOUSEHOLD WAS AT SAN JOSE IN 1885 AND AT MONTEVIDEO IN 1886 ***, where his son Eduardo was born on 22 April. *** THOSE TWO BIRTHS ARE ELEVEN MONTHS APART, which is possible and tight, and is recorded as a tension rather than resolved. *** *** AND IN 1909 HE AND HIS WIFE ARE GIVEN AT DIFFERENT ADDRESSES *** - he at calle Colonia *** 2200 ***, she at calle Colonia *** 228 *** - both 'de estado casado'. The numbers differ by a factor of ten and the likeliest reading is a transcriber's slip rather than a separation; *** NOT RESOLVED. *** *** HIS WHOLE KNOWN SIBSHIP, FROM ONE PARENT-PAIR QUERY - 12 October 2026. *** Six children by Emma Regules: *** EMA JUSTINA FELICIA (b. 18 May 1881, San Jose), ARTURO MARIO (b. 9 April 1884, San Jose, who died at Montevideo in 1949), EMMA (b. 18 May 1885, San Jose), EDUARDO (b. 22 April 1886, Montevideo), CORA MARIA AVELINA (b. 8 June 1887, christened at the Union 23 October 1887) and ROBERTO AMBROSIO (b. 1 November 1896, Montevideo) ***. *** AND TWO OF THOSE NAMES CORROBORATE HIS OWN PARENTAGE WITHOUT A SECOND ACT. *** The 1880 marriage makes him a son of *** AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***; his fifth child is *** AVELINA *** and his sixth is *** AMBROSIO ***. *** A HOUSEHOLD NAMES ITS CHILDREN FOR ITS OWN PARENTS, and this one did it twice. *** *** THE FAMILY MOVED: *** San Jose from 1881 to 1885, Montevideo from 1886. *** AND THERE IS A NINE-YEAR GAP, 1887 to 1896 ***, which in a household of this period usually means children this query did not reach - deaths in infancy, or acts indexed under another spelling. *** HIS DEATH ACT, AND IT IS THE BEST DOCUMENT THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS - 12 October 2026. *** *** 'En Montevideo y el dia DOS DE MARZO DE MIL NOVECIENTOS TREINTA Y SEIS... declarando que a las DOS HORAS del dia de hoy y en TREINTA Y TRES 269, fallecio ARTURO LERENA, del sexo masculino, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDO EN MONTEVIDEO, de SETENTA Y OCHO ANOS DE EDAD, de estado casado, DE PROFESION ABOGADO, a consecuencia de [la causa] segun consta del certificado del DOCTOR JORGE CALVETTE... Que el finado era HIJO DE A[V]ELINO [L]ERENA y de AMBROSIA TR[A]IBEL, AMBOS FALLECIDOS... era casado con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS llamados EMA, MARIO, EDUARDO, CORA y ROBERTO.' *** *** SO: d. 2 March 1936, at two in the morning, at Treinta y Tres 269, aged 78, a lawyer. *** The act confirms his parents a second time and confirms the profession correction made the same day. *** AND IT NAMES FIVE SURVIVING CHILDREN WHERE THE INDEX GAVE SIX. *** Ema, Mario, Eduardo, Cora and Roberto - which is this register's sibship with *** ONLY ONE EMA ***. That does not settle the two daughters born on 18 May, in 1881 and 1885: five surviving of six is what the act would say if one had died. *** IT DOES TILT IT *** - see the rows for both women. *** THE AGE IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT STATEMENT OF HIS BIRTH YEAR AND THEY ALL AGREE: *** twenty-two in June 1880, sixty-two in January 1920, seventy-eight in March 1936 - 1857, 1857-58, 1857-58. *** AGAINST ONE BAPTISM OF A 'JUAN ARTURO' IN FEBRUARY 1861. *** *** FAMILYSEARCH'S OWN TREE HAS ALREADY MERGED THEM ***, attaching this death record to a profile 'Juan Arturo Lerena Traibel, 1861-1936'. *** THAT IS A TREE, NOT A DOCUMENT ***, and this register keeps the two apart until an act does the joining. *** THE DECLARANTS WERE NOT FAMILY: *** an Italian employee of forty and an oriental of twenty-three, neither named Lerena, which is the ordinary shape of a city death registration and means the ages in it are secondhand.

The act records *** 'el finado era casado con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS' *** - so she outlived him, or at least was not recorded as dead, which is not the same thing and is all the act says.

name: BARBARA (enslaved in Alejandro Lerena's household, San Jose 1846)

note: *** SHE WAS NOT A WIFE AND SHE WAS NOT A LERENA. SHE WAS AN ENSLAVED WOMAN, and this archive published her as somebody's spouse for a few hours on 12 October 2026. *** The index of her son's burial lists 'Alejandro Lerena' as father and 'Barbara Lerena' as mother, and on that reading this register entered a Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple. *** THE PLATE SAYS OTHERWISE: *** *** 'En esta Parroquia de S.n Jose a VEINTE Y OCHO DE ABRIL de mil ochocientos CUARENTA Y SEIS, yo D.n FRAN.CO CASTELLO cura vic.o int.o di sepultura en el ANGELORIO al cadaver de CARMELO ANSELMO, HIJO NATURAL DE BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA, murio ayer de enfermedad, de edad de SIETE DIAS, y se le hizo oficio rezado, de que certifico.' *** *** 'ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA' - THE INDEXER TURNED THAT INTO A MARRIAGE, giving her the surname of the man who held her. *** She is named here as the act names her: *** BARBARA, with no surname ***, because the act gives her none and this archive will not lend her one. *** HER SON WAS CALLED CARMELO ANSELMO AND HE LIVED SEVEN DAYS. *** He is entered as *** 'hijo natural' ***, which is what the act says; no father is named on it. *** THE FIFTH PERSON THIS FAMILY IS KNOWN TO HAVE HELD IN SLAVERY. *** The others are JUANA, ANTONIO, JOSE and TERESA, in Sancho Llerena's household at Canelones in 1812, with Juana's daughter MARIA MERCEDES born into it. *** THIS ONE IS THIRTY-FOUR YEARS LATER AND IN A DIFFERENT HOUSEHOLD. *** *** ON THE DATE, THIS ARCHIVE STATES ONLY WHAT IT KNOWS: *** the act says 'esclava' in April 1846. name: Dr LLERENA (curador, Buenos Aires courts 1889)
source: Aguirre, Feliciano: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1889, the Agente Fiscal's dictamen - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 12 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSTZ-396J-K
note: *** A LERENA PRACTISING IN THE BUENOS AIRES COURTS, AND HE IS NOT THE WORD 'HERENCIA'. *** This archive's worklist carried him as a one-line snippet with a warning attached, because in that corpus *** lerena *** is very often the transcriber's reading of *** herencia ***. He is real. The Agente Fiscal's opinion in the Feliciano Aguirre probate reads: *** '...no lo hace el DOCTOR LERENA si la intervencion del CONSUL ESPANOL en este estado del juicio es o no oportuna. Lo que debe resolverse es si el nombramiento del CURADOR DON LLERENA es o no arreglado a derecho. Al simple pedido de [Contreras] de f.46, el Juzgado nombra CURADOR AL DOCTOR LLERENA, sin oir a este Ministerio... hubiera dictaminado que se librase nuevo oficio al Senor CONSUL DE ESPANA, para que si deseare intervenir en este juicio lo hiciere dentro de un termino perentorio.' *** *** SO: A LAWYER APPOINTED CURADOR OF AN ESTATE, AND THE FISCAL IS COMPLAINING THAT THE COURT APPOINTED HIM WITHOUT ASKING THE MINISTRY OR THE SPANISH CONSUL. *** The consul's interest means the deceased was most likely a Spanish subject. *** THE SAME PASSAGE SPELLS HIM BOTH LERENA AND LLERENA ***, twice each, in one hand - which is the single clearest demonstration in this register that the two spellings are one name. *** AND HE IS NOT A PHYSICIAN. *** 'Doctor' before a curador is the style of an ABOGADO, the same lesson this archive learned about Arturo Lerena of Montevideo earlier the same day. *** A 'DOCTOR LERENA' RECURS IN THIS COURT ACROSS A DECADE *** - the Regidor probate of 1890, Villaverde-Duportal 1894 and Foz 1897 all carry the phrase and *** NONE OF THEM HAS BEEN OPENED. *** *** NOT MERGED WITH CARLOS A. LERENA ***, the commission agent who sued the Escalada estate in the same courts in February 1890: one is a party suing, the other an officer of the court, and nothing joins them but a surname and a city.

[SUPERSEDED 18 October 2026: HER HUSBAND IS RAMON FERNANDEZ, named in the baptism of their daughter below.] *** THE INDEX GIVES TRINIDAD AS HER BIRTHPLACE *** while the family is at San Jose in 1825 and 1829; that is probably where she died, and is unresolved. *** A BAPTISM OF HER OWN IS FOUND AND READ AT THE PLATE, 18 October 2026: MARIA CASILDA, CHRISTENED AT SAN JOSE ON 11 APRIL 1827. *** 'En once de Abril de mil ochocientos veinte y siete, yo el Dr. D.n Feliciano Rodriguez, Cura y Vicario Interino de esta Parroquia, bautice solemnemente a Maria Casilda, hija legitima de Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez. Abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria de Leon. Maternos Juan [y] Barbara Sotura. Padrinos Marcos de Leon Gonzalez y [Maria] Fernandez Albarez, a quienes instrui y por verdad lo firme'; margin 'Maria Casilda'. NO BIRTH DATE IS WRITTEN, so she was born on or before that day. *** THE IDENTIFICATION: *** the parents are Alexandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez and the grandparents Ramon and Maria [de Leon / Gonzalez] and Juan and Barbara Sotura - the same four lines as her siblings' baptisms - and she is the ONLY Maria of Alejandro and Margarita known to this register; the 1892 death act names the same parents and no more than 'Maria Lerena de Fernandez', sixty-four. So Maria Casilda is the Maria of 1892 on every particular that can be compared, and nothing contradicts it - STRONG, NOT PROVED: no document names her husband and no baptismal name appears in 1892. *** SHE IS THE ELDEST OF THE FIVE *** and the only one born before Alejandro's baptism volume begins. *** THE GODFATHER IS 'MARCOS DE LEON GONZALEZ', *** carrying the 'de Leon Gonzalez' of her paternal grandmother's family (the 1812 and 1816 acts have Maria Josefa / Maria de Leon Gonzalez, daughter of Marcial de Leon Gonzalez): a kinsman on her father's mother's side, not placed here. The godmother is Maria Fernandez Albarez - the SISTER of Margarita who stood at her wedding in 1825, named on this register as Margarita's sister Maria. The index gave Trinidad as her birthplace; she was baptised at San Jose, and Trinidad is where she died. *** HER NAME: MARIA CASILDA WAS NAMED FOR HER AUNT CASILDA FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ, 18 October 2026, *** the wife of her godfather Marcos de Leon Gonzalez, who is her father's mother's brother. *** HER HUSBAND IS NAMED, 18 October 2026: RAMON FERNANDEZ - AND HE IS HER FIRST COUSIN. *** The Trinidad baptism of their daughter, read at the plate, 'En diez y nueve de Julio de mil ochocientos cincuenta y siete, Yo Florentino Luis Conde, Cura Vicario de la misma, bautice solemnemente a Maria del Carmen [del Corazon de Jesus], que nacio el dia diez y seis del que rige, e hija legitima de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Lerena, naturales y vecinos de esta Parroquia. Abs. Pat.s Manuel Fernandez y Maria de los Reyes Gonzales, Mat.s D.n Alejandro Lerena y D.a Margarita Fernandez, y fueron los Pad.s Serapio Fernandez y Socorro Lerena, a quienes adverti el parentesco espiritual y demas oblig.s'. *** SO MARIA LERENA, 'DE FERNANDEZ' IN 1892, WAS THE WIFE OF RAMON FERNANDEZ, A SON OF MANUEL FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ - MARGARITA'S BROTHER - AND MARIA DE LOS REYES GONZALEZ, *** so she and Ramon were first cousins on her mother's side, exactly as her sister Socorro and Serapio Fernandez were (Serapio is another son of Manuel). Two sisters married two brothers who were their first cousins. Both couples were 'naturales y vecinos' of Trinidad in 1857. *** THE DAUGHTER MARIA DEL CARMEN WAS BORN 16 JULY 1857 *** and her godparents were her aunt Socorro and uncle Serapio. *** THE DISPENSATION IS FOUND, 19 October 2026 [the sentence that stood here, 'not found', is superseded]. *** Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1852-1855, film 007713344, item 3 (images 162-167), expediente no. 15 of 1853. The cover (image 162, plate read): 'Don Manuel Fernandez por su hijo Ramon, solicita ... dispensa del impedimento canonico de parentesco en segundo grado de consanguinidad por linea transversal con Maria Lerena: parroquia de Porongos'. THE PETITION (image 164, plate read): Manuel Fernandez, married, of the 'Partido nombrado las Puntas de San Jose', in the parish of the Santisima Trinidad in the Porongos, says that by his marriage to Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez he has a son Ramon, 'soltero, de edad de veinte y un anos, nativo y domiciliado' in that district, who with his father's consent means to marry 'la joven mi sobrina Maria Lerena, de edad de veinte y cuatro anos, natural de San Jose, y domiciliada en la campana del territorio de mi indicada parroquia, hija legitima de Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez, que es mi hermana', Manuel and Margarita being children of Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura: 'primos hermanos, ligados en segundo grado de consanguinidad por linea transversal'. THE CAUSES HE GIVES (machine transcript; the rest of the petition was not read at the plate): she is older than twenty-four; she lives in an unpopulated place where she cannot easily find another man she is not related to; she has no dowry; her parents are burdened with a family - 'nueve hijos, entre estos cuatro mujeres'; and a young woman there is exposed to being carried off. THE GRANT (images 165-166, machine transcript): the Provisor General's decree at Montevideo on 7 September 1853 (notary Sebastian Roso) ordered a genealogical diagram and the same day dispensed 'Ramon Fernandez y Maria Lerena, parroquianos de la ... Iglesia de Porongos', on condition that three witnesses swear before the Cura y Vicario of the parish to the descent from Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura, the two marriages, her age, her poverty and the size of her parents' family, with a penance of three pounds of wax each for the lamp of the Blessed Sacrament; the entry is registered at folio 40 of the third book (image 167). THE DIAGRAM (image 163, plate read, 7 September 1853): Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura at the apex; below them 'Manuel' (hijo) and 'Margarita' (hija) as 'hermanos, 1.o g.o'; below those Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena as 'primos hermanos, 2.o g.o'. *** WHAT IT CHANGES: *** the kinship is no longer worked out here from baptisms; it is stated by the parties' own papers - Maria is the niece of Manuel Fernandez and the first cousin of Ramon, through her mother Margarita, Manuel's sister. *** HER STATED AGE IS A YEAR OR TWO LOW, AS IT WAS IN 1892: *** 'veinte y cuatro' in September 1853 would be a birth in 1828 or 1829, and the baptism puts it on or before 11 April 1827; the petition itself lists 'older than twenty-four' as its first cause, so the figure is a round statement and is not used for her birth. *** NINE CHILDREN, FOUR OF THEM GIRLS, IN 1853, *** where this register holds five by name (Maria, Alejandro, Estefania, Socorro, Bernabe): if the nine count her, one more daughter and three more sons of Alejandro and Margarita are unplaced. *** RAMON'S AGE: *** twenty-one in 1853, so born about 1832 and some five years younger than his wife. *** NOT FOUND: *** the marriage act itself (after 7 September 1853 and before July 1857, at Trinidad), the three witnesses' depositions, and Ramon's death before 1892. *** HER AGES, HER HUSBAND'S ACT AND HER CHILDREN, 19 October 2026: *** the civil act of 27 October 1887 (Trinidad, no. 93; see her husband's row) calls her 'Dona Maria Lerena, Oriental, de cincuenta y ocho anos de edad', married to Ramon Fernandez, with 'tres hijos mayores de edad'. So her age is given as 24 (September 1853), 58 (October 1887) and 64 (May 1892): all three point to a birth in 1828 or 1829, one to two years after the baptism's 'on or before 11 April 1827'. The baptism is the better record, and the stated ages are the usual rounding; a second Maria born in the 23 months between Alejandro (February 1829) and Estefania (January 1831) is not excluded by anything held here, so the identification stays STRONG, NOT PROVED. *** HER CHILDREN: *** Maria del Carmen (born 16 July 1857); Ramon the younger (about 1860; married Maria Serna at Trinidad on 18 October 1894, the act calling him 'hijo legitimo de Don Ramon Fernandez de Dona Maria Lerena'); and a third, Jesus Modesto del Carmen, born in January 1866 (below). *** HER SISTER NATALIA, 19 October 2026: *** a Natalia Lerena is godmother with Ramon Fernandez on 21 August 1858 (the baptism of Hipolito Fructuoso, son of Socorro and Serapio), and 'Natalia Lereña', wife of Manuel Vaquero, has two sons baptised at Trinidad in 1862 and 1866 with Alejandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez as godparents of the first: she is Maria's sister and the fourth of the 'cuatro mujeres' of the petition of 1853 (Maria, Estefania, Socorro, Natalia). Strong, not proved: no act says 'daughter of Alejandro and Margarita'. *** A WARNING ON GODPARENTS: *** another Ramon Fernandez, with a wife 'Maria Teresa', stood godparent at Trinidad in 1863 and 1864 and had a daughter in May 1862 (the plate reads 'Maria Teresa Santiles', the index agrees); the 1868-1886 godparent entries below name 'Maria Lerena', but only 1886 is tied to the family. *** SHE IS VERY LIKELY THE MARIA LERENA WHO STOOD GODMOTHER WITH RAMON FERNANDEZ AT TRINIDAD ON 16 JULY 1868, 15 JULY 1879 AND 4 MAY 1886 *** and who is named with him as a witness at a marriage of 14 August 1877 (names only, machine transcripts). Her sister Estefania's husband Servando Gonzalez made the declaration of 27 October 1887. *** HER FIRST CHILD IS BORN IN AUGUST 1855, 25 October 2026: *** 'Eusebio Ramon ... que nacio el [day cut] de este mes y ano, hijo legitimo de Ramon Fernandez y Maria Leiena', baptised 18 August 1855 by the Don Miguel Ramos with Margarita Fernandez as godmother by proxy - the first of the household, born within two years of the dispensation of 7 September 1853, so the marriage act lies between that grant and the summer of 1855, a narrower window than 'September 1853 to 1857'. *** TWO MORE CHILDREN, 26 October 2026: *** Maria Josefa del Carmen, baptised 22 May 1862 (mother written 'Maria Lorena'), and Modesta Carmelita, born 24 February 1864 and baptised 4 March, whose entry gives the grandparents: 'Paternos Manuel Fernandez y [Maria de los] Reyes; Maternos Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez' - a third act that names Maria's parents. With Eusebio Ramon (1855), Maria del Carmen (1857), Ramon (1859) and Jesus Modesto (1866) she has six children baptised at Trinidad. *** SHE BURIED THREE CHILDREN IN 1873, 26 October 2026: *** Modesta Carmelita (5 May), Maria Josefa del Carmen (26 May) and Maria de los Reyes, a baby of fourteen months (10 August); the Trinidad burials name 'Ramon y Maria Serena'. Her last known child is Maria de los Reyes, born about June 1872, named for her husband's mother, who died at Trinidad on 20 December 1884. *** HER PARISH BURIAL, 4 MAY 1892, 27 October 2026: *** the entry, whose close stands at the head of image 26 (plate read): '... se hizo el oficio de sepultura al cadaver de Maria Serena [Lerena] que fallecio ayer a la edad de sesenta y cuatro anos, oriental, viuda de Ramon Fernandez. Recibio el Santo Sacramento de la Penitencia', signed Manuel Brana. It agrees with the civil act no. 49 of 3 May 1892 and with her baptism of April 1827 (sixty-five); and it says in a priest's hand that Ramon Fernandez was dead before 3 May 1892. *** GODMOTHER WITH RAMON FERNANDEZ ON THREE ACTS OF 1878-79, 29 October 2026: *** the Maria Lerena who stands beside Ramon Fernandez at three Trinidad baptisms, twice 'representada' by another woman. (Machine transcripts, images 159, 217, 232.) *** HER PARENTS NAMED, 15 MARCH 1868, 29 October 2026: *** the baptism of her daughter Victoriana del Carmen (born 6 March 1868) gives the maternal grandparents as Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez; the paternal as Manuel and Maria Reyes Gonzalez. And a Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena stand godparents in June 1868 (images 68-69). (Machine transcripts.) *** NAMED IN TWO ACTS OF 1885, READ AT THE PLATE, 29 October 2026: *** she stands in for her husband Ramon Fernandez as godparent on 1 September 1885 (written Lerena, page 462, no. 347), and on 15 October 1885 is godmother with him and maternal grandmother of Bruno Arsenio Gonzalez (written Serena, page 472, no. 385). She may be this woman or a niece or namesake; nothing joins them and she is not entered separately. *** SHE IS A SISTER OF ALEJANDRO LERENA THE ELDER AND THE WIFE OF FRANCISCO FERNANDEZ, 19 October 2026. *** The baptism of 1 May 1828 of Pedro Francisco, born 29 April 1828, names his parents as 'Francisco Fernandez y Clara Lerena', his paternal grandparents as 'Juan, y Barbara Solera [Sotura]' and his maternal grandparents as 'Ramon y Maria de Leon Gonzalez' - the grandparents of Alejandro's children too - with Marcos de Leon Gonzalez and Casilda Fernandez as godparents; later entries make 'Don Francisco Fernandez y su esposa Dona Clara Ledena' godparents (1833, 1835) and 'Clara Lerena' godmother again in 1831, 1834, 1835, 1838 and 1859-1862 at Trinidad. So the 'Clara Llerena' who stood godmother to Alejandro the younger in 1829 is his aunt or sister: Alejandro's mother Maria is a de Leon Gonzalez, and Clara, daughter of the same Ramon and Maria, is his father's sister, so his AUNT. She married a brother of her brother's wife. *** GODMOTHER AT TRINIDAD IN FEBRUARY 1852, 25 October 2026: *** 'padrinos Don Manuel Ferregra y Dona Clara Lerena' to Juan Manuel, born 8 February 1852, natural son of Martina Caceres - the same Manuel who stood with Socorro in 1849. *** SHE STANDS GODMOTHER AT TRINIDAD ON 7 OCTOBER 1858 TO FRANCISCO REMIGIO FERNANDEZ, 26 October 2026, a son of Francisco Fernandez and Fulgencia Romero, *** and again in October 1861 and June 1862 - the first of them to the child of a couple who held her nephew Venancio in May 1858. *** GODMOTHER IN MAY 1825, FOUR MONTHS BEFORE HER BROTHER'S MARRIAGE, 26 October 2026: *** 'siendo sus padrinos Yo dicho Cura y Clara Pereña' to Pascual Maria Cruz, a newborn girl of Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez - so she stood godmother to her own youngest sister. *** SHE DIED ON 16 AUGUST 1886, AT EIGHTY-ONE, 26 October 2026. *** The burial entry, read at the plate: 'El dia diez y siete de Agosto de mil ochocientos ochenta y seis, se hizo el oficio de sepultura al cadaver de Clara Lerena que fallecio ayer a la edad de ochenta y un anos, oriental, viuda de Francisco Fernandez. Recibio los Santos Sacramentos de la Penitencia y Extremauncion', signed Manuel Brana. *** SHE IS THE CLARA OF THE ROW ABOVE, ON THE HUSBAND'S NAME AND THE AGE (born about 1805, which makes her the elder sister of Alejandro, as the 1825 godmother of her youngest sister implied), AND IT IS AN IDENTIFICATION BY NAME, NOT A MERGE OF ANY ROW. *** Not reconciled: the Trinidad burial of 28 August 1884 of Manuel Ferreira, a Brazilian of sixty-eight, is worded in the machine's text 'casado con Dona Clara Lorena' (image 169, plate not opened) - the godfather who stood with Clara Lerena in 1852 may be he, and whether a Clara Lerena took a second husband or the clerk wrote the wife of another man is not settled here. *** HER SON FRANCISCO DIED ON 18 MARCH 1894, 27 October 2026: *** the civil act of 19 March 1894 gives a Francisco Fernandez, sixty-five, as 'hijo legitimo de Don Francisco Fernandez y de Dona Clara Lerena, fallecidos' (plate read) - the Pedro Francisco of 1828 very probably - and calls her dead eight years after her burial of 17 August 1886.

note: *** SON OF RAMON FERNANDEZ AND MARIA LERENA, FOUND 19 October 2026. *** The Trinidad marriage act of 18 October 1894 (machine transcript): 'Don Ramon Fernandez Oriental, soltero, de treinta y cuatro anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Don Ramon Fernandez de Dona Maria Lerena; con Dona Maria Serna, Oriental y soltera, de veintitres anos de edad, hija legitima de D. His two stated ages, thirty-four in October 1894 and forty-two in March 1902, are eight years apart across seven and a half; the rounding of the clerks. *** HIS BAPTISM IS FOUND, 19 October 2026: BORN 14 AUGUST 1859, CHRISTENED 19 AUGUST AT TRINIDAD. *** Entry no. 123: 'bautice solemnemente a Ramon de la Asuncion Fernandez que nacio el quatorce de este mismo mes y ano, hijo legitimo de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Llerena, Orientales. Fueron Padrinos Manuel Fernandez y Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez', the cura Facundo Bonamino - so his godparents are his father's parents, as María del Carmen's were her mother's brother and sister. His stated ages (34 in October 1894, 42 in March 1902) agree with 1859 within a year. *** AND HIS OWN END IS INDEXED, 19 October 2026: *** 'Ramon A. Fernandez Lerena', 51, born 1860, a Montevideo civil act of 5 March 1911 (no. 139) giving a death of 4 March 1911, with the spouse 'Apolinaria Sena' - which ties the Apolinaria Sena of the 1902 acts to him by a third paper. note: *** RAMON LERENA'S FIRST WIFE, FOUND 26 October 2026, AND THE TREE'S 'MARGARITA LEAL'. *** At Rosario del Colla on 16 May 1789 Ramon Llerena, son of Salvador Llerena and Ana Cubas of Valdemoro, married 'Margarita Leal, natural del Tucuman, Obispado de Cordova, viuda de Pedro Cabrera' (plate read), with Sebastian Gonzalez and Magdalena Fuentes of the bishopric of Buenos Aires as witnesses.
